## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## Owner statements 2026-11-20 (third) — the project is a database and a pipeline, kept as simple as possible; the content of the CLAUDE.md rewrite

Given in the session `session_2026-11-20-unregistered-map-codes` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iQWmsqeLLsdnXfD7Pu), in typed messages while the coordinator reported an Opus adjudication of the core against the machinery and an antagonist audit of it. Derive the times from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "as simple as possible in infrastructure" -- transcripts`).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "this entire infrastructure is just trying to formalize asking a Claude session to do research on a topic"
>
> "i have just spent a huge amount of time trying to harness an LLM through gates/scripts/github/etc instead of just using it to translate things i can't read"
>
> "all i want is for the information to be properly recorded in a database"
>
> "that's it"
>
> "and then we squeeze it through a pipeline"
>
> "i am just saying that the heart of this project really isnt that complicated"
>
> "overall we need to make this project as simple as possible in infrastructure because the more exceptions we have the more complexity we guard against which is the more we spiral"

The goal sentence of the same session is quoted in the entry "Owner statements 2026-11-20 — translation runs before judgment …" (`grep -n -F "we research, we record, we verify we recorded things accurately" references/project-standards.md`) and is not repeated as a second home.

**The content of the CLAUDE.md rewrite, recorded so a later session can write it.** Source: the Opus adjudication of 2026-11-20 and the antagonist's audit of it, read by the coordinator. **This is a proposal. The owner has not approved it, and `CLAUDE.md` is unchanged by this entry.** Its sections, in order:

1. **Goal.** The owner's goal sentence verbatim, then one line: a thinking tool, not an authority; the database records research properly and a pipeline processes it; `base` is the owner's request layer, standing where the owner would otherwise ask for a topic directly.
2. **The things never to get wrong.** (a) Fetch before you write any author, title or figure; a bibliographic field is never written from memory when a payload is in hand. (b) Keep the original text, unit and clause beside every translated figure, and show the owner an English rendering that records who or what translated it and when; an English rendering is never written into `claimed_value` or `claimed_unit`. (c) The disabled people who co-produced a work are evidence and stay credited (Co-1).
3. **The six verbs and the command for each** (research, record, verify, evaluate in context, synthesize, show), one line each.
4. **The write path,** in one sentence (rule 3).
5. **Derive, do not type, a number** (rules 7a and 8, condensed).
6. **Pointers** to doctrine, the tier system, the rulings ledger and the working-rules file.

**Moved to a referenced working-rules file:** rules 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10; section 3 (the layers and the spine); section 7 (traps); section 8. **Deleted:** the Layer-0 preamble, rule 7 (merged into 7a), the sentence that the stage display form is derived by `stage_label()` (no such function exists: `git grep -n stage_label -- scripts governance .claude skills` finds none), and the embedded "Proof" narratives (`git log -p CLAUDE.md` holds them).

**Two constraints the audit found.** `scripts/audit/claude_md_spine.py` pins the SPINE line, so that line stays in `CLAUDE.md` or the blocking check moves with it. Comments in scripts cite `CLAUDE.md` rules by number (for example "rule 4", "section 5(c)"), so renumbering breaks them silently; sweep them first (rule 4 names prose callers as unswept). **Size,** measured and never typed: `[ $(wc -w < CLAUDE.md) -le $(( $(git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md | wc -w) / 4 )) ]`.

**What the owner approves, and what a session may do.** The owner approves the goal sentence, rule 0, rule 9, the tier and Co-1 definitions, and the fate of the layer model. A session may reorder and reword process rules, traps and command lists.

**The simplicity rule these words state, for any session that adds anything:** each addition names the existing thing it replaces or deletes and what reads it; a new exception is a reason to change the rule, not to add a guard (CLAUDE.md section 8 already says the first half).

CONDITION: any session editing `CLAUDE.md`, adding a table, verb, check, script or exception, or planning the remediation work.
ACTION: (1) Do not rewrite `CLAUDE.md` until the owner approves the content above; then write it from this entry and the audit, with the size command. (2) Before adding apparatus, state what it replaces and what reads it. (3) Treat the proposal's sections and moves as unratified until the owner's words approve them.
DATE: 2026-11-20 — owner statements (typed words, quoted above); the rewrite content is the coordinator's record of the audits, not an owner statement.

## Owner statements 2026-11-20 (fourth) — one large pull request for the remediation work; the identity, need and ICF matrix ships on its own

Given in the session `session_2026-11-20-unregistered-map-codes` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iQWmsqeLLsdnXfD7Pu), in two typed messages sent while the coordinator was carrying out the plan of the open work (translation, units, verification, the CLAUDE.md rewrite, housekeeping) as an ordered sequence of small pull requests with stop points. Derive the times from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "just do a big pull request" -- transcripts`).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "no, just do a big pull request so i don't have to waste time"
>
> "the matrix can be on its own"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "a big pull request" covers the whole remaining plan of the open work except the matrix: translation before judgment, units, verification, the CLAUDE.md rewrite and the housekeeping, with their tooling and the research rows they need in the same pull request — basis: the words, and "so i don't have to waste time" (fewer review points)].
- [ASSUMPTION: "the matrix" is the judged identity, access-need and ICF table of T-145 and the rows that fill it, and "on its own" is a separate pull request, tooling first as T-145 says — basis: the entry "Owner statement 2026-11-20 (second)"].
- [ASSUMPTION: the owner's words supersede, for this one pull request and on contact (rule 0), the separation of research from tooling in CLAUDE.md rule 10; the rule stands for every other pull request — basis: a live owner statement naming one big pull request].
- Nothing here approves the CLAUDE.md rewrite's content; the pull request carries it for the owner's review, with its rule 0 and rule 9 text moved and not changed, and the pull request description names it as the part the owner approves by merging.

CONDITION: any session shaping the pull request or pull requests for the work of the entry "Owner statements 2026-11-20 — translation runs before judgment …" or the remediation plan of 2026-11-20.
ACTION: (1) Ship that work as one pull request, with the matrix excluded; ship the matrix as its own. (2) Order the commits inside the pull request tooling first, then the rows they enable, so each commit stands on the one before. (3) Keep the checks of each part in the same pull request and report any that cannot go red on the defect. (4) Treat the assumptions above as unratified except where the owner's words state them.
DATE: 2026-11-20 — owner statements (typed words, quoted above).

## Owner statements 2026-11-20 (fifth) — the identity, need and ICF matrix holds all three keys; a qualitative value cell may be corrected in place (GAP-368)

Given in the session `session_2026-11-20-core-work` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMXTj2zDxrGgKjkaLX), in typed messages answering the coordinator's two owner questions after an Opus adjudication of eight decisions and an antagonist's critique of it. Derive the times from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "should be all three" -- transcripts`; `git grep -n -F "you can correct in place" -- transcripts`; `git grep -n -F "Yes @ T-145" -- transcripts`).
----
## Owner statement 2026-11-25 (seventh) — CLAUDE.md's goal should say the project is simple and builds as little machinery as possible

Given in the session `session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary` (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMXTj2zDxrGgKjkaLX), in a typed message after the coordinator waited on an independent check of the Opus adjudication. Derive the time from the preserved transcript (`git grep -n -F "build as little machinery as possible" -- transcripts`). Recorded on contact (rule 0).

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "maybe claude.md goal should also state this is a simple project where we build as little machinery as possible to enact our goal"

**Readings.**

- [ASSUMPTION: "maybe" invites the edit and does not forbid it, so the coordinator made it: a sentence in CLAUDE.md's Goal section quoting the owner's words and pointing at section 8 — basis: the words; the owner may replace the wording, and merging approves it, as the entry on the Goal section of pull request 243 said].
- The sentence adds no rule and no check; it states the owner's standing direction (section 8, "Minimise code") where every session reads it first.

CONDITION: any session reading CLAUDE.md's Goal section.
ACTION: (1) Meet the goal with the least machinery; apply section 8's order to every task. (2) Treat the reading above as unratified except where the owner's words state it.
DATE: 2026-11-25 — owner statement (typed words, quoted above).

## Delegated resolutions 2026-11-25 (second) — the referred-back questions ruled for the smallest change: no pairs table, the repeated rows kept, the 29 pairs classed, the doubted mapping held and T-128 withdrawn, no body-function proposals, SCI retired into WHEEL, carry-only batches gated by their own tests (OD-73, OD-77, OD-78, OD-82, OD-83 to OD-87)

Written by the coordinating session from the adjudication of an Opus-class instance (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-22-icf-umbrella-glossary/adjudication-2.md`) under the owner's words of 2026-11-25 ("Opus to adjudicate all of the above and log it"; "I don't want to answer these right now so just make it happen"; "Remember that this project is simple!!!"; entry "Owner statements 2026-11-25 (sixth)"), after an independent check by a different instance, whose corrections are applied below. **Not an owner statement.** The schema ties `stated` and a retirement to an "Owner" ledger entry; no ruling here is one, none writes such a heading, and no guard is relaxed.

**OD-73 (a pair of an identity and an access need before any ICF code): no pairs table; "should be all three" stands.** "We should be able to map them to one another" is met by `identity_need_icf` as it is: a pair is a row whose ICF code is one of the need's own `access_need_icf` codes, which the owner ruled counts as the identity's ICF coverage (2026-11-21, sixth). "Perhaps, we select ICF codes" means further rows for a pair with a body-function or activity code where one is grounded. Nothing is built. Basis: the 2026-11-20 (fifth) and 2026-11-21 (sixth) answers; CLAUDE.md section 8.
OD-73 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-73 CHECK: confirmed

**The 63 rows that repeat a need's own codes: kept.** They are the coverage the owner ruled (2026-11-21, sixth), and under OD-73 the record of each pair; that ruling is the later and more specific one on these rows (rule 0). Retiring them would need an "Owner" `retirement_ref`. Derive: `select count(*) from identity_need_icf t where retired_at is null and exists (select 1 from access_need_icf a where a.need_code=t.need_code and a.icf_code=t.icf_code)`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pin CLAUDE.md's SPINE line to governance/pipeline-contract.yaml.

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK IF THIS DOES NOT EXIST (CLAUDE.md §1).
The stage list is the frame rule 5 is applied against: you cannot tell a
legitimate stage-specific fact from a copy without knowing which stage a table is
in. CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded into every session, so when its stage list drifts
from the contract, every table-to-stage judgement made that session is made
against the wrong map -- and the wrong answer is a duplicated fact in the
database, not a red check.

This is not hypothetical. The five-stage list of 2026-08-25 was superseded by a
six-stage list on 2026-08-27 and by the seven-stage spine (D-0167) the same day;
for thirteen days CLAUDE.md carried BOTH "Substrate is not a stage" and, forty
lines below, the paragraph recording that the machine enforces `base` as one.
One file, two answers, and no check could see it because the list was prose.

WHY THE CONTRACT IS THE PARENT. governance/pipeline-contract.yaml's `stages:` is
the declared single home of the stage ids (rule 5). CLAUDE.md renders it for a
reader; a rendering that disagrees with its source is the defect.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

import yaml

CLAUDE_MD = "CLAUDE.md"
CONTRACT = "governance/pipeline-contract.yaml"
SPINE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*SPINE:\s*(.+?)\s*$", re.M)
SEP = " -> "


def main() -> int:
    for path in (CLAUDE_MD, CONTRACT):
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"FAIL: missing {path}")
            return 1

    text = open(CLAUDE_MD, encoding="utf-8").read()
    found = SPINE_RE.findall(text)
    if len(found) != 1:
        print(f"FAIL: expected exactly one SPINE: line in {CLAUDE_MD}, found {len(found)}")
        print("      The line is the checked rendering of the contract; do not hand-edit or duplicate it.")
        return 1

    declared = [s.strip() for s in found[0].split(SEP)]
    contract = [str(s["id"]) for s in yaml.safe_load(open(CONTRACT, encoding="utf-8"))["stages"]]

    print(f"EXAMINED: {len(contract)} contract stage(s) against 1 SPINE line")
    if declared != contract:
        print("FAIL: CLAUDE.md's SPINE line disagrees with the contract, which is the single home.")
        print(f"  CLAUDE.md : {SEP.join(declared)}")
        print(f"  {CONTRACT}: {SEP.join(contract)}")
        print("  Correct CLAUDE.md, or change the contract first if the spine itself was re-ruled.")
        return 1

    print(f"PASS: SPINE matches {CONTRACT} — {SEP.join(contract)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#

# turn by design:
#
#     transcripts/harness_*/main.jsonl          grows when the agent writes anything
#     scratchpad/<session>/commands.jsonl       grows on every Bash call

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py — GAP-290 enforcement.

Rebuilds a fresh DB from the migration history alone and compares core invariants
against the committed data/guidebook.db. A divergence means someone wrote directly
to the DB and bypassed the migration system, so the committed blob no longer
reproduces from its own history.

WHY THIS IS A SCRIPT
--------------------
It used to exist twice — as an inline heredoc in .github/workflows/audit.yml and  [RETIRED-VOCAB-OK]
a second, separately-maintained heredoc in scripts/preflight.sh. Two copies of an
invariant list is one copy too many: adding a table to one does not add it to the
other, and nothing would have told you. This is now the single definition, wired
through governance/check-registry.yaml.

SCOPE (DR-2026-05-28 / D-4.3-H option 3a, ratified 2026-06-11)
--------------------------------------------------------------
The gate enforces the CORE INVARIANTS below. They cover all synthesis-bearing
content and must reproduce from migration history.

No table is exempt. The last exemption, `evidence_source_authors`, ended when the divergence the
scheduled job left in it was reverted (plan steps 1.5 to 1.5c).

Checks:
  C1  the migration history rebuilds without error

branch slug. Batches 11–15 wrote branch slugs and their rows were stamped
`session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-...` — a mismatch that scopes any check reading

**THE FOLDER NAME AND `CURRENT`'S CONTENT MUST BE IDENTICAL, not just similar.**
`.claude/hooks/record-command.py` only honours `CURRENT` when
`scratchpad/<CURRENT's content>` is a real directory; otherwise it falls back to a
same-harness-sid guess that can misfile the whole command log into an unrelated past
session's folder (measured 2026-09-27, ~30 minutes of commands lost into a stale
directory after a session changed `CURRENT` to the stem without renaming its folder to
match). Create the folder AS the stem from the start — never a bare slug — so there is
no window where they disagree:

```
SLUG="${1:-$(git branch --show-current | sed 's|.*/||')}"
STEM="session_$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)-${SLUG}"
mkdir -p "scratchpad/$STEM"
echo "$STEM" > scratchpad/CURRENT
cat scratchpad/CURRENT
```

(CLAUDE.md section 7), so the hook never meets a `CURRENT` that names no folder.

51:**Universality requirement.** A skill file describes a protocol Claude executes when invoked. The protocol is generic over inputs: it cites no specific session IDs, no specific dates, no commit SHAs, no specific gaps, no embedded changelog. Project-specific state that the skill operates on lives in the database or in DRs the skill references by stable identifier. If a skill cannot be authored without specific project state, the state belongs in the PI rule that invokes the skill, not in the skill itself.
53:**Placeholder convention.** When PI references a skill that does not yet have a file, the PI states "skill placeholder" or "no skill file exists" inline so the absence is intentional rather than a bug.

def open_session(root, sid=None):
    """Stem of the session running NOW, derived. '' when it cannot be told.

    THE 2026-08-23 FIX WAS WRONG AND THIS RECORDS WHY, because the wrong version
    is the plausible one and will be reached for again.

    Until 2026-08-23 this hook read `.claude/session`. That pointer went stale and
    filed one session's commands under the previous session's scratchpad. The fix
    swapped it for `sessions/LATEST` on the ground that LATEST is "the single home
    for this fact". IT IS NOT. LATEST answers *which session record is most recent*
    and is moved BY THE CLOSE-OUT RITUAL — so for the entire life of a session it
    names the PREVIOUS one. Both pointers were stale in exactly the same way and
    for exactly the same reason; swapping which stale pointer you read changed
    nothing. MEASURED 2026-08-25, in the file the fix was supposed to protect:

        scratchpad/session_2026-08-23-research-batch-03-forward-mining/commands.jsonl
            5 lines dated 2026-08-23   <- its own session
          405 lines dated 2026-08-24   <- session_2026-08-24-pointer-discipline
          274 lines dated 2026-08-25   <- session_2026-08-25-rulings-...-sweep

    Three sessions, one file, named after the earliest. The two later sessions have
    scratchpad directories of their own and NO commands.jsonl in them. That defeats
    the owner directive the whole hook exists to serve (2026-08-20, "the scratchpad
    needs to be getting saved always for provenance"; 2026-08-25, "so that we
    actually have a surface to review") -- a surface filed under another session's
    name is not a review surface, and it corrupts that session's frozen record too.

    So DERIVE it instead, from a fact already stated once, with no new pointer:

        A SESSION IS CLOSED EXACTLY WHEN ITS RECORD sessions/<stem>.md EXISTS.

    A scratchpad/session_* directory with no record behind it is therefore OPEN,
    and the newest open one is the session running now (stems are date-prefixed by
    convention, so lexical order is chronological). Verified against the same three
    sessions: 08-23 has a record and is closed; 08-24 and 08-25 have none, which is
    exactly why their lines had nowhere correct to go.

    LIMIT, stated rather than discovered later: stems are date-prefixed, so lexical
    order is chronological ACROSS days but arbitrary WITHIN one. Two sessions opened
    on the same UTC day and both left un-closed tie on alphabet. That case resolves
    by closing sessions out, not by making this cleverer -- 08-21-reasoning-doc-

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

BASE="origin/main"
ARGS=()
MODE_ALL=0
USER_KINDS=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --base)  BASE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --all)   MODE_ALL=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      sed -n '2,44p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
      exit 0 ;;
    # An explicit --kinds means the caller has chosen the work kinds themselves,
    # so appending --changed-from would hand run_checks.py two contradictory
    # sources of truth. It refuses that combination (deliberately — silently
    # discarding one of them is how a real diff came to report "0 changed
    # files"), which would have made `preflight.sh --kinds X` permanently exit 2.
    --kinds) USER_KINDS=1; ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
    *)       ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

if ! python3 -c "import yaml" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "preflight: PyYAML is required — pip install -r requirements.txt" >&2
  exit 2
fi

echo "===== preflight: registry selftest ====="

content.content:
echo "===== preflight: registry selftest ====="
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest || exit 1
echo

if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BASE" >/dev/null; then
  echo "preflight: base ref '$BASE' not found; fetching..." >&2
  git fetch origin main --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
  if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BASE" >/dev/null; then
    echo "PREFLIGHT: NOT RUN — base ref '$BASE' does not exist (a run that names a base it cannot read is not a gate)"
    exit 2
  fi
fi
if [ "$MODE_ALL" -eq 1 ]; then
  python3 scripts/run_checks.py --all --base "$BASE" ${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}
elif [ "$USER_KINDS" -eq 1 ]; then
  python3 scripts/run_checks.py --base "$BASE" ${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}
else
  python3 scripts/run_checks.py --changed-from "$BASE" ${ARGS[@]+"${ARGS[@]}"}
fi
status=$?

echo
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "PREFLIGHT: PASS — safe to push."
  echo "  (gated on your diff — run 'scripts/preflight.sh --all' for the full battery.)"
elif [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; then
  echo "PREFLIGHT: NOT RUN — run_checks.py refused the selection (exit 2); read its message above."
else
  echo "PREFLIGHT: FAIL — fix the blocking failures above before pushing."
  echo "  (stale context map? run: python3 scripts/generate/context_map.py)"
fi
exit "$status"

915 .claude/README.md
# `.claude/` — what lives here and why

The contract for this directory. It holds **harness wiring only**: things the
Claude Code runtime loads on its own, without an agent choosing to. Project
doctrine lives in `governance/`, process in `CLAUDE.md`, and the research
protocol in `skills/`.

**The organising principle, and it is this repository's own.** From
`.claude/settings.json`, on why the 2026-07-24 research run skipped Co-1,
citation mining, clause citation and combinatorial pairing while the rules for
all four sat documented:

> the rules did not fail; PROSE failed — an agent must choose to load it, and
> attention degrades as context fills.

So the test for putting something here is not "is this important?" It is: **does
this have to work when nobody remembers it?** If an agent must choose to read
it, it belongs in `governance/` or `skills/` and it is not enforcement.

---

## Layout

| Path | Loaded by the harness | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.json` | always | permissions and hooks |
| `hooks/` | fired by `settings.json` | the scripts hooks run |
| `agents/` | on `Agent` dispatch | subagent definitions, one per file |
| `commands/` | on `/<name>` | slash commands for repeated workflows |
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | on `Skill` dispatch | **symlinks** into `skills/` |

not a licence to bypass; the capture set is `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)`, and a table it misses is a defect fixed
there. Exception (owner, 2026-11-21): a qualitative value or wording cell may be corrected by hand in a data migration,
with the old value, the new value, the reason and the session recorded in the migration header and in the gap's
resolution. Identifiers, keys, vocabularies, counts and bibliographic fields stay behind their writers; ask before
extending the exception to any other column.

**`db.py` refuses, and that is its whole value.** A writer that merely INSERTs is worse than hand SQL because it looks
safe. One refusal is deliberately absent and must stay absent: `add-population-match` does not enforce uniqueness on
(ref_id, population), so a dissenting adversarial grade lands as a second row and divergent grades read as a contest.

**Schema shape (owner, 2026-11-06): one value per cell, and each fact in the cell that names it.** A list, a JSON
array, a delimited string, a prefix that says what the rest of the cell means, or a correction appended to a note is
data joined in a cell or in the wrong one; give each kind its own column (a foreign key where a table exists) and each
repeated value its own row. Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after a schema change.

**Vocabularies come from the schema, not a list in code.** `dbcore.check_values()` reads the column's own CHECK; live
rows are a *sample* of a vocabulary, never the vocabulary. **Never compute a ref_id by hand** —
`dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` (`python3 scripts/db.py next-id ref`) takes the high-water mark over the UNION of every
table holding a ref_id.

**Schema change:** a new `scripts/migrations/NNN_slug.sql` that bumps `user_version`. Verify with
`python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild /tmp/rebuilt.db`.

`FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` at INSERT, never at migration time, so the schema looks healthy, a rebuild reproduces
it, and every gate stays green over a table that cannot accept a row. Derive the UNWRITABLE set before planning any
write — the `db-census` agent, or the probe in `.claude/agents/db-census.md` — and never quote it.

## 5. The three failure modes that are real

**(a) A gate that passes having examined nothing.** Every check must print `EXAMINED: <n>`; `run_checks.py` reports
zero-subject passes as NOTHING-IN-SCOPE and escalates blocking-and-vacuous ones. **When a check passes, confirm it had
a subject.**

**(b) Prose that contradicts the database.** See rules 7 and 7a.

**(c) A fabricated citation passing green gates.** A gate that asks whether author fields are *populated* passes
invented authors — including the erasure of a Co-1 paper's disabled co-authors. **Verification must leave an
artefact:** `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` logs every retrieval as a manifest line (URL, time, status, byte count,
sha256), and `--verify-authors` diffs stored data against the logged payload. An artefact a search-execution or
admission gate must find is committed; a large PDF, page or extracted text is logged by where it was retrieved from,
not committed (owner, 2026-11-06).

## 7. Traps

- **A publisher block (403, a JS challenge, a new paywall) is not terminal — try the Internet Archive (research contract
  R10).** `curl -sS "http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<host+path, no scheme>"` finds a snapshot; fetch it as
  `https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<original URL>` (the raw file, and the form the egress proxy lets
  through). On a connection reset, retry once and try the plain `/web/<timestamp>/` form. Persist what comes back
  through `retrieval_log.fetch()`. Resets on every form while a known-good control URL also fails are a session-level
  proxy limit, not a missing snapshot.
- **`.ignore` hides frozen records from ripgrep and the Grep tool**; its entries are the list (`cat .ignore`). **Owner
  rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`.** `git grep`, `grep -r` and a Glob that names the directory see through
  it. **Never report a ruling absent from a search that could not have seen it.**
- **`scratchpad/CURRENT` names the session running now, and it moves at OPEN.** `sessions/LATEST` and
  `LATEST-RESEARCH` move at CLOSE, so both name the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of the current one. `CURRENT`
  holds the DB session stem (`session_YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`), and its scratchpad folder must be named identically;
  `/session-open` sets both. If your PR merges mid-session, move `CURRENT` and the folder together, in one action, or
  the command log is misfiled.
- **Session ids: bare stem in the DB, `.md` in pointers and `emit_data_migration --session`.** The wrong form scopes a
  gate to nothing and it passes green.
- **`git rebase` and `git checkout -B` are blocked in this harness.** `git merge origin/main` reaches the same state
  without rewriting history.
- **THE ITEM LAYER IS GONE FROM THE DATABASE AND STILL LIVE ON THE READING SURFACE.** `references/` and `working/` still
  publish prior-version item codes whose names state their answers (`E-08 Corridor Clear Width (≥1200 mm Minimum on
  All Primary Routes)`). The owner deleted the layer because *"if E-08 already exists then the work is predisposed to
  filing into a container that already exists, and that biases every finding."* **Treat every `[A-Z]-NN` code you meet
  as prior-version content, never as a container to file into.** Derive the live surface before framing anything:
  `grep -rEl '\\b[A-Z]-[0-9]{2}\\b' references/ working/`
- **If you add a `SessionStart` hook, APPEND it — never insert at index 0.** `research_contract_hook.py` reads
  `SessionStart[0]["hooks"][0]["command"]` by index; an insert turns the blocking `research_contract_sync` red.
- **PI versioning is intentional**: the numerically highest `governance/project-instructions-v*.md`
  (`ls governance/project-instructions-v*.md | sort -V | tail -1`) serves the claude.ai surface and lags doctrine.
  Prefer the ledger and recent DRs.
- **Don't run `scripts/bootstrap.sh`** — PAT-gated, for the claude.ai surface.
- **TWO TRACKED FILES APPEND ON EVERY TURN** — `transcripts/harness_*/main.jsonl` and
  `scratchpad/<session>/commands.jsonl` — so any "is the tree clean?" gate is unsatisfiable while a session is live. Do
  not answer the harness stop hook with a commit when only these two are dirty; commit them at a natural break (rule 6).
  The real question is `git diff --quiet -- :/ ':(exclude)transcripts/' ':(exclude)*commands.jsonl'`. SessionStart runs
  `scripts/fix_stop_hook_loop.sh` silently to teach the hook that exclusion; whether it took:
  `grep -c stophook.ignorePath ~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh`.

## 8. Deleting is as cheap as adding

**Adding apparatus carries the burden of proof; removing it does not.**

- **Code, checks, scripts, dead tables and views: delete them.** No owner gate. You need *evidence* — unreferenced,
  vacuous after a real batch, or superseded — not permission. Record it in the commit.
- **Git history is the archive for CODE.** Do not copy scripts to `_archived/`; it is for retired reader-facing
  *content*.
- **Owner sign-off is required for content and doctrine only** — the list in `governance/decision-protocol.md` §2.4.
  Code is not.
- **Before adding a check, script or table, state what wrong thing reaches the *guidebook* if it does not exist, and
  name what reads it.** If the answer is about the apparatus rather than the book, do not add it. An unread field, an
  uncalled script and an unregistered check are the same defect.
- **Minimise code** (owner, 2026-10-12 and 2026-11-06: the minimum that performs the action correctly). Try, in order:
  do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest
  code that closes the defect. A PR touching `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` names what the added code
  reads, what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it, and any existing code it replaces or makes deletable. A
  writer that refuses what it should, a typed column in place of a convention, and a test that can go red are not
  waste. Measure: `git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'`. Enforced
  by review, not by a check.
- **A specific, ratified authorisation beats a blanket caution.**

Adding a check means editing `governance/check-registry.yaml` — never a workflow. It is the single inventory;
`run_checks.py` is the only thing that invokes a check.

# CLAUDE.md — working guide for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook

## Goal

The owner's goal, verbatim (2026-11-20): *"we research, we record, we verify we recorded things accurately, we
evaluate things in context with other related things, we synthesize then show"*.

**The project is simple** (owner, 2026-11-25: *"this is a simple project where we build as little machinery as possible to enact our goal"*; also *"Remember that this project is simple!!!"*). Meet the goal with the least machinery: §8's order applies to every task, and a table, verb, check or rule that the goal does not need is not built.

The project is a database that records research properly, and a pipeline that processes it; `base` is the owner's
request layer, standing where the owner would otherwise ask for a topic directly. The owner reads only English, so
three things are never to be got wrong:

1. **Fetch before you write any author, title or figure.** A bibliographic field is never written from memory.
2. **Keep the original beside every translated figure,** and show an English rendering that records who translated
   and who reviewed it, and when (`translations`; `db.py translations --show` prints each reviewed one beside its
   original); never English into `claimed_value` or `claimed_unit`.
3. **Co-1 co-producers are evidence and stay credited.**

A reference on architecture, accessibility and built-environment standards centred on **disabled
people**. Fixed doctrine: a **thinking tool and advocacy project, not an authority** — *"the purpose
of this guidebook is to get people to ask the right questions."* Not a prescription manual, not a
legal authority, not a substitute for professional judgment. "Inclusive / accessible / universal"
here always means *inclusion of persons with disabilities*.

**Authority, highest first:** (1) the owner's words, live or quoted verbatim in `references/project-standards.md`
(rule 0; a recorder's `[ASSUMPTION]` reading is not one); (2) owner answers and ratifications; (3) delegated
resolutions, within their recorded reach; (4) ratified records — decision records (`decisions/DR-2026-08-19-…` among
them), ledger RULEs and canonical `governance/` documents, as amended by their appended notes, the later on a point
winning; (5) this file; (6) plans and task files; (7) frozen records (`sessions/`, `transcripts/`, `_archived/`), which
bind nothing by themselves.

This file holds **process, workflow and rules only**; every volatile fact is derived, never stated (rule 7a). When a
sentence here is found wrong, fix the sentence and put the account of the error in the commit message;
`git log -p CLAUDE.md` is the record. Every line here is paid for on every turn.

---

## 1. Run these first

`/orient` starts any session; run `/session-open` before the first Bash call of a batch (§7). SessionStart runs
`.claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`, which exits 0 even when it fails, and without `pydantic` the governance battery is red
on untouched `main`: check `python3 -c 'import pydantic, jsonschema'` before believing a red result. **Never
`pip install -r requirements.txt`** (its PyYAML pin cannot replace the system copy, so nothing lands); install packages
individually. The dependency list's one home is `governance/check-registry.yaml`'s `batteries:`.

```
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list     # registry + quarantine (runs nothing)
scripts/preflight.sh                     # THE gate: registry selftest, then the checks your diff vs origin/main warrants
scripts/preflight.sh --explain           # the same, with why each check was or was not selected
```

**Run the gate once, when the diff is ready to open a PR** (owner, 2026-09-23: *"stop running suites so frequently …
interrogate their merits"*), and never re-run a check when nothing it reads has changed. A targeted question takes
`run_checks.py --battery <name> --kinds <kinds>` (or `--battery <name> --changed-from origin/main`): read `selected N
of M`; exit 2 means the selection was refused or matched nothing. `--all` is for a corpus-wide question only. A bare
`run_checks.py --changed-from` skips the selftest, where a rename fails (rule 4). Before trusting a green result, ask
whether the check could have gone red on the defect in front of you; one red on untouched `main`, or one that examined
nothing (§5(a)), tells you nothing about your diff.

**Use the project's own agents and commands before general-purpose ones.** Agents in `.claude/agents/`: `repo-sweep`
for rule-4 caller sweeps and derived counts, `db-census` for row counts and the UNWRITABLE set (§4), `antagonist` for
the adversarial pass. Commands in `.claude/commands/`: `/orient`, `/session-open`, `/adversarial` after substantive
work, `/batch-done` as the only definition of "finished". Before invoking a skill, check that it does not presuppose
the deleted item layer (§7).

---

## 2. The rules that stop you

Each rule names what enforces it. **"NOT ENFORCED" means you are the gate.**

**0. A live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches, on contact.** Record
the supersession; never weigh the ruling against the paperwork it changes. A DR, a RULE, an ADOPTED
directive are what a ruling *changes* — never an argument against it. Numbered 0 because the rest of
this file tilts the other way.
*Proof: on 2026-08-18 the owner ruled `axes` a bad coined term, marked "do not relitigate", and the
next day a batch framed four of five searches on bare `axis_code`, hiding a second mechanism.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `supersession_backpointer_audit`, for supersessions a `SUPERSEDES` line
names. Naming them is yours.

`run_checks.py --battery <name> --kinds <kinds>` (or `--battery <name> --changed-from origin/main`): read `selected N
of M`; exit 2 means the selection was refused or matched nothing. `--all` is for a corpus-wide question only. A bare
`run_checks.py --changed-from` skips the selftest, where a rename fails (rule 4). Before trusting a green result, ask
whether the check could have gone red on the defect in front of you; one red on untouched `main`, or one that examined
nothing (§5(a)), tells you nothing about your diff.

**Use the project's own agents and commands before general-purpose ones.** Agents in `.claude/agents/`: `repo-sweep`
for rule-4 caller sweeps and derived counts, `db-census` for row counts and the UNWRITABLE set (§4), `antagonist` for
the adversarial pass. Commands in `.claude/commands/`: `/orient`, `/session-open`, `/adversarial` after substantive
work, `/batch-done` as the only definition of "finished". Before invoking a skill, check that it does not presuppose
the deleted item layer (§7).

---

## 2. The rules that stop you

Each rule names what enforces it. **"NOT ENFORCED" means you are the gate.**

**0. A live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches, on contact.** Record
the supersession; never weigh the ruling against the paperwork it changes. A DR, a RULE, an ADOPTED
directive are what a ruling *changes* — never an argument against it. Numbered 0 because the rest of
this file tilts the other way.
*Proof: on 2026-08-18 the owner ruled `axes` a bad coined term, marked "do not relitigate", and the
next day a batch framed four of five searches on bare `axis_code`, hiding a second mechanism.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `supersession_backpointer_audit`, for supersessions a `SUPERSEDES` line
names. Naming them is yours.

**1. Commit format.** `{skill-name}: {action} [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]`, timestamp last, from
`date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'`. Use `governance` when no project skill fits.
→ Enforced by `scripts/ci_helpers/check_commit_msg.py` on **push events only** (the `commit-msg` job of
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); never on a PR.

**2. Attestation on synthesis paths.** A changed `.md` file under `references/connection-reasoning/`, `decisions/` or
`sessions/` needs `attestations/<dir>_<stem>.json`, valid against `schemas/attestation.schema.json`.
→ Enforced by `attestation_presence` and `attestation_schema` (both blocking). **No gate reads the free text for
meaning**; you are its gate.

**3. Never write `data/guidebook.db` directly.** Migrations only, by the write path of §4. Committed migrations are
append-only and immutable: fix forward with a compensating migration.
→ Enforced by `migration_reproducibility` (blocking), **which compares row COUNTS only** — an UPDATE is invisible to
it. `migration_reproducibility_deep` compares every row and is **advisory**.

**4. A rename or removal is not done until the callers are swept.** **A VIEW IS A CALLER. So is a skill, the check
registry, and prose.** Grep `sqlite_master` as well as the tree, and **treat a 0-row object as unproven, not clean.**
After changing any checked value or name, `git grep` `governance/`, `references/`, `architecture/`, `scripts/`,
`skills/` and `.claude/` for sentences restating it.
→ Enforced by `schema_reference_audit` (blocking) for names that must resolve in the schema, and by
`run_checks.py --selftest` C7 for registry basis refs. **Prose callers are not covered.**

**5. Never write the same fact into a second table. Point, do not copy** (owner, 2026-08-24: *"It is better to have a
table cell point to another table cell than to rewrite."*). Each stage (§3) holds only its own data and reaches earlier
stages by pointer on the shared reference ID. **A parity check is not a fix**: it makes a dual home permanent. To drop
a column a committed data migration INSERTs, the schema migration must replay after every one of them (an
`-- AFTER_DATA:` line, read by `migrate_db.build_plan()`): grep `scripts/migrations/data_*` first, then retire the
writer, then the readers, then NULL forward.
→ **NOT ENFORCED — you are the gate.**

**6. Commit the scratchpad AND the agent transcripts at every natural break**, not at session end.
`python3 scripts/preserve_transcripts.py` copies transcripts out of ephemeral `~/.claude/projects`, which a fresh clone
does not inherit (the SubagentStop hook runs it for subagents; committing is yours); `--check` says what is
unpreserved. If no session directory exists, create it (`/session-open`). `governance: session command log
[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]` is a complete commit message.
→ **NOT ENFORCED, deliberately.** `--check` is red for the whole life of a session, and a check that is red by
construction teaches its reader to ignore it.

**7. No hand-written counts.** Derive every volatile fact — row counts, schema version, CI state, the active plan —
from the live repo; where a figure cannot be generated, stamp it with its date and a drift warning.
→ **NOT ENFORCED — you are the gate.**

**7a. A NUMBER IS WRITTEN AS THE COMMAND THAT COMPUTES IT, NOT AS ITS RESULT** (owner, 2026-09-16) — in a document, a
comment, a registry entry, a commit message or a criterion. Where the number must also appear, the command stands
beside it and the reader is told to re-run rather than trust. **Ask of every figure you are about to type: could this
be wrong tomorrow with nothing going red?** If yes, it is hard-coded, whatever its shape — a literal, a threshold, a
`min_items`, a list, a glob, or a sentence.
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED.** `run_checks.py --selftest` C9 falsifies a `no_floor` reason that claims an empty subject over a
live one. **Everywhere else, prose above all, you are the gate.**

**8. DERIVE IT, OR NAME WHO JUDGED IT. Never curate a fact the machine can compute.** A vocabulary comes from the
column's own CHECK; an ordering from the live FK graph; an identifier from the union of its homes; a tier from the
ladder; the set of writable tables from the writers — never from a list kept beside the thing it describes. **Where
judgment IS genuinely required, the script asks for it**, constraining the answer to the live vocabulary, demanding
the evidence, and recording the answer and its warrant in named columns. The model fills a field. It never invents a
value or a vocabulary term, and never supplies a number the schema could have computed.
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `dbcore.check_values()` (vocabularies), `identifier_floor_audit` (identifiers),
`dbcore.writable_tables()` (the capture set) and `adjudication_integrity` (tiers);
`python3 scripts/audit/derived_not_curated_audit.py` judges the shapes it covers — run it, and do not count violations
by grepping `choices=`. Otherwise you are the gate: look for a typed list that duplicates a column's CHECK.

**9. Do not watch PRs. Open the PR last** (owner instruction, 2026-09-23). Do not call
`subscribe_pr_activity` (either server's) and do not schedule `send_later` or `create_trigger`
check-ins: this is the owner saying the PR is not to be watched, which the harness's default-subscribe
instruction defers to. **Creating a PR subscribes the session by itself** (observed on #158: a
`subscription.created` event arrived with no subscribe call), so call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for
it immediately after `create_pull_request`, before anything else. Open the PR once, when the diff-scoped gate (§1) is clean and the work is
finished, and push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change. A commit that only carries the
append-only logs (§7) goes in with the work, or carries `[skip ci]` before the timestamp. The final
push to a PR is never `[skip ci]`, or its head has no CI result. The owner reads CI on GitHub.
*Proof: in the 2026-09 transcripts most wake-ups on subscribed PRs were a CI run reporting green,
and each did no work but still cost a full-context turn. The batch that opened its PR at the end
used a fraction of the tokens of the batch that opened early.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** once the owner adds both `subscribe_pr_activity` tools, `send_later` and
`create_trigger` to `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json`: that stops explicit subscription
and polling, but not the subscription PR creation makes, so the unsubscribe step is yours. Never
deny `unsubscribe_pr_activity`. `ci.yml`'s `concurrency` block
cancels superseded runs, which saves runner time but does not stop a wake-up.

**10. Research and the tooling it uses ship apart.** A schema migration, a new `db.py` verb, a new check — anything
Layer 0/1/2 (§3) — goes in a tooling-only PR, merged to main first; a research batch's rows go in their own PR after.
A writer gap discovered mid-batch is filed as a GAP and either left unwritten or written through verbs the CLI already
has; it is never patched with hand SQL inside the batch's data migration. `data/guidebook.db` shipping with a
schema-only migration (no `data_*.sql` file alongside) is the ordinary shape of a schema bump, not a violation.
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `research_tooling_separation` (advisory). It classes `governance/check-registry.yaml` as
`governance`, so a registry entry landing new tooling beside research rows is invisible to it.

---

## 3. The layers, and the spine

**Owner ruling 2026-09-09** — the project is five layers:

> **Layer 0** is Claude.md and tools/scripts that ensure that Layer 1's architecture/shape/pipelines/schema etc are working
> **Layer 1** is code architecture and data shape and pipeline orchestration and schematic compliance etc — it is what guides all processes in the pipeline
> **Layer 2** is comprised of each stage in the pipeline including its tools/workflows/processes/scripts etc
> **Layer 3** is the actual data being recorded in the tables
> **Layer 4** is supplementary data

Full record: `references/project-standards.md`, 2026-09-09.

**THE CANONICAL SPINE. This line is checked; do not hand-edit it.**

    SPINE: base -> research -> evidence -> judgment -> synthesis -> specification -> render

`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`'s `stages:` is the single home of the stage ids; the line above is a rendering of
it, and `base` is the vocabulary layer the machine gates as a stage.
→ Enforced by `claude_md_spine` (blocking). Never spell the stages out a second time in this file.

| Stage | Holds |
|---|---|
| **base** | The vocabularies and registries every other stage points into |
| **research** | What was searched, screened and mined, plus the clue store |
| **evidence** | What was admitted, its identity and its verification |
| **judgment** | What each source asserts for each parameter (the extraction), whether it is sound, and how it weighs |
| **synthesis** | What the judgments say together — weighing, convergence, cross-slug findings |
| **specification** | The determination: *therefore 1200 mm, marked ●* |
| **render** | Book surfaces, read from the database when rendered (owner, 2026-08-27); no committed file is one |

**Rule 5 is unusable without this table.** Table-to-stage judgments live in `governance/stage-map.yaml`. **A
cross-stage view IS the pointer** — a view joining two stages on the shared reference ID is what "point" means in SQL
— **and is therefore the most protected object in the schema: before deleting any view, ask which stages it spans.**
Every stage points into `base`, so a view reading one stage plus `base` is not counted as crossing. A walk may
re-enter an earlier stage (a reasoning document can yield research leads); that is write order, not what a table may
hold.

---

## 4. Writing the database

`data/guidebook.db`, SQLite, committed as a binary blob. `PRAGMA user_version` is the schema version.
**There is no `sqlite3` CLI** — use Python, read-only:

```python
import sqlite3
con = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
```

**THE WRITE PATH IS ONE SENTENCE:** scratch copy → `scripts/db.py` subcommands →
`scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py` → `scripts/emit_data_migration.py` → `scripts/migrate_db.py`.
`cp data/guidebook.db $SCRATCH`, then point `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` at it **inline on every call** — the harness resets env
between shells. The canonical DB's sha256 must not move until the migration is applied.

**Do not hand-write SQL against a table the CLI can reach.** If you find one it cannot, that is a coverage bug to fix,
not a licence to bypass; the capture set is `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)`, and a table it misses is a defect fixed
there. Exception (owner, 2026-11-21): a qualitative judgment or wording cell may be corrected by hand in a data migration,
with the old value, the new value, the reason and the session recorded in the migration header and in the gap's
resolution. Ask the owner before treating any other kind of column as qualitative.

**`db.py` refuses, and that is its whole value.** A writer that merely INSERTs is worse than hand SQL because it looks
safe. One refusal is deliberately absent and must stay absent: `add-population-match` does not enforce uniqueness on
(ref_id, population), so a dissenting adversarial grade lands as a second row and divergent grades read as a contest.

**Schema shape (owner, 2026-11-06): one value per cell, and each fact in the cell that names it.** A list, a JSON
array, a delimited string, a prefix that says what the rest of the cell means, or a correction appended to a note is
data joined in a cell or in the wrong one; give each kind its own column (a foreign key where a table exists) and each
repeated value its own row. Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after a schema change.

**Vocabularies come from the schema, not a list in code.** `dbcore.check_values()` reads the column's own CHECK; live
rows are a *sample* of a vocabulary, never the vocabulary. **Never compute a ref_id by hand** —
`dbcore.next_ref_id(conn)` (`python3 scripts/db.py next-id ref`) takes the high-water mark over the UNION of every
table holding a ref_id.

**Schema change:** a new `scripts/migrations/NNN_slug.sql` that bumps `user_version`. Verify with
`python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild /tmp/rebuilt.db`.

**A NOT NULL foreign key into an EMPTIED table makes that table unwritable.** The refusal comes only at INSERT, so the
schema looks healthy, a rebuild reproduces it and every gate stays green. Derive the UNWRITABLE set before planning
any write (the `db-census` agent; its file holds the probe), and never quote it.

---

## 5. The three failure modes that are real

**(a) A gate that passes having examined nothing.** Every check must print `EXAMINED: <n>`; `run_checks.py` reports
zero-subject passes as NOTHING-IN-SCOPE and escalates blocking-and-vacuous ones. **When a check passes, confirm it had
a subject.**

**(b) Prose that contradicts the database.** See rules 7 and 7a.

**(c) A fabricated citation passing green gates.** A gate that asks whether author fields are *populated* passes
invented authors — including the erasure of a Co-1 paper's disabled co-authors. **Verification must leave an
artefact:** `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` logs every retrieval as a manifest line (URL, time, status, byte count,
sha256), and `--verify-authors` diffs stored data against the logged payload. An artefact a search-execution or
admission gate must find is committed; a large PDF, page or extracted text is logged by where it was retrieved from,
not committed (owner, 2026-11-06).

---

## 6. Evidence model

`governance/tier-system.md` is operative. **T1** primary controlled research · **Co-1** lived
experience / participatory design, **co-primary with T1** under CRPD Art 4.3 · **T2** synthesis ·
**Co-2** OT professional-body CPGs · **T3** grey primary · **T4–T6** the regulatory stratum, walled
off from full-strength anchoring.

Markers: **●** confirmed · **◐** policy/standards only · **○** grey, thin or unverified (the source could not be retrieved). Unmarked is an error.
Cell states: the `specifications.state` CHECK (`dbcore.check_values`). No row is stored for a parameter and lens a
determination does not concern (owner, 2026-10-29, OR-1).

**Co-1's warrant is co-production.** The disabled people who produced the work are part of the
evidence, not metadata. Erasing them while claiming the tier is the worst failure available here.

Work from the **ICF/access-need frame with codes AND names**, never bare codes, never population umbrellas. **The
crossing is JUDGMENT's output** (owner, 2026-08-27): harvest concepts at evidence (`db.py observe-term`, verbatim and
unjudged), adjudicate at judgment. Zero links **after judgment** is a defect. Only an Opus-class model or above (Fable-class
included; `governance/decision-protocol.md` §4.2; owner, 2026-07-25) writes a determination (`specifications`).

**Both halves of the determination's key are RULED.** Subject: the canonical parameter, `parameter_id` (owner,
2026-08-26; read its five-clause ACTION before touching any of this: `grep -n 'judgment object is the'
references/project-standards.md`); `items` is a render rollup derived from specifications, never a key. Lens: at least
one of the identity, ICF and access-need columns, with real FKs (owner, 2026-08-28, as relaxed by D-0182);
`population_code` and the medical lens are retired. `slug × population` is no part of the key: `base_taxonomy_identity`
IS the identity lens, and that key is the traversal D-0184 rejected. Verify with `PRAGMA table_info(specifications)`,
and search for both halves of a question before calling either open.

---

## 7. Traps

- **A publisher block (403, JS challenge, new paywall) is not terminal (research contract R10).** Find a snapshot with
  `curl -sS "http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<host+path, no scheme>"` and fetch
  `https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<original URL>`; on a connection reset, retry once and try the plain
  `/web/<timestamp>/` form. Persist what comes back through `retrieval_log.fetch()`. Resets on every form while a
  known-good control URL also fails mean the session's proxy, not the snapshot.
- **`.ignore` hides frozen records from ripgrep and the Grep tool**; its entries are the list (`cat .ignore`). **Owner
  rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`.** `git grep`, `grep -r` and a Glob that names the directory see through
  it. **Never report a ruling absent from a search that could not have seen it.**
- **`scratchpad/CURRENT` names the session running now, and it moves at OPEN.** `sessions/LATEST` and
  `LATEST-RESEARCH` move at CLOSE, so both name the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of the current one. `CURRENT`
  holds the DB session stem (`session_YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`), and its scratchpad folder must be named identically;
  `/session-open` sets both. If your PR merges mid-session, move `CURRENT` and the folder together, in one action, or
  the command log is misfiled.
- **Session ids: bare stem in the DB, `.md` in pointers and `emit_data_migration --session`.** The wrong form scopes a
  gate to nothing and it passes green.
- **`git rebase` and `git checkout -B` are blocked in this harness.** `git merge origin/main` reaches the same state
  without rewriting history.
- **THE ITEM LAYER IS GONE FROM THE DATABASE AND STILL LIVE ON THE READING SURFACE.** `references/` and `working/` still
  publish prior-version item codes whose names state their answers (`E-08 Corridor Clear Width (≥1200 mm Minimum on
  All Primary Routes)`). The owner deleted the layer because *"if E-08 already exists then the work is predisposed to
  filing into a container that already exists, and that biases every finding."* **Treat every `[A-Z]-NN` code you meet
  as prior-version content, never as a container to file into.** Derive the live surface before framing anything:
  `grep -rEl '\b[A-Z]-[0-9]{2}\b' references/ working/`
- **If you add a `SessionStart` hook, APPEND it — never insert at index 0.** `research_contract_hook.py` reads
  `SessionStart[0]["hooks"][0]["command"]` by index; an insert turns the blocking `research_contract_sync` red.
- **PI versioning is intentional**: the numerically highest `governance/project-instructions-v*.md`
  (`ls governance/project-instructions-v*.md | sort -V | tail -1`) serves the claude.ai surface and lags doctrine.
  Prefer the ledger and recent DRs.
- **Don't run `scripts/bootstrap.sh`** — PAT-gated, for the claude.ai surface.
- **TWO TRACKED FILES APPEND ON EVERY TURN** (`transcripts/harness_*/main.jsonl`, `scratchpad/<session>/commands.jsonl`),
  so a "tree clean?" gate is unsatisfiable while a session is live. Do not answer the harness stop hook with a commit
  when only these are dirty; commit them at a natural break (rule 6). The real question is
  `git diff --quiet -- :/ ':(exclude)transcripts/' ':(exclude)*commands.jsonl'`. SessionStart runs
  `scripts/fix_stop_hook_loop.sh` silently to add that exclusion to the hook; whether it took:
  `grep -c stophook.ignorePath ~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh`.

---

## 8. Deleting is as cheap as adding

**Adding apparatus carries the burden of proof; removing it does not.**

- **Code, checks, scripts, dead tables and views: delete them.** No owner gate. You need *evidence* — unreferenced,
  vacuous after a real batch, or superseded — not permission. Record it in the commit.
- **Git history is the archive for CODE.** Do not copy scripts to `_archived/`; it is for retired reader-facing
  *content*.
- **Owner sign-off is required for content and doctrine only** — the list in `governance/decision-protocol.md` §2.4.
  Code is not.
- **Before adding a check, script or table, state what wrong thing reaches the *guidebook* if it does not exist, and
  name what reads it.** If the answer is about the apparatus rather than the book, do not add it. An unread field, an
  uncalled script and an unregistered check are the same defect.
- **Minimise code** (owner, 2026-10-12 and 2026-11-06: the minimum that performs the action correctly). Try, in order:
  do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest
  code that closes the defect. A PR touching `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` names what the added code
  reads, what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it, and what existing code it replaces or makes deletable;
  refusing writers, typed columns and tests that can go red are not waste. Measure:
  `git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'`. Enforced by review.
- **A specific, ratified authorisation beats a blanket caution.**

Adding a check means editing `governance/check-registry.yaml` — never a workflow. It is the single inventory;
`run_checks.py` is the only thing that invokes a check.

---

## 9. Where to look

Single author, pre-launch. Query the database for the real state.

| Question | Read |
|---|---|
| What to do now | the ACTION lines of the newest entries at the tail of `references/project-standards.md`, and the plan they name |
| Latest owner rulings | the tail of `references/project-standards.md` |
| Research rules | `governance/research-contract.yaml` (the SessionStart hook injects it) |
| Doctrine | `governance/mission-and-epistemics.md` |
| Tiers, markers, weighting | `governance/tier-system.md`, `governance/evidence-architecture.md` |
| Stages and their criteria; which stage a table is in | `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`; `governance/stage-map.yaml` |
| The schema | `sqlite_master` and `PRAGMA table_info` (§4) |
| ICF codes and the three lenses | §6; `python3 scripts/db.py icf-glossary` |
| Who decides what | `governance/decision-protocol.md` (§2.4 lists what only the owner decides) |
| Checks | `governance/check-registry.yaml`; `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list` |

**History, not live guidance:** `governance/conceptual-model.md` (built on the deleted item layer),
`governance/functional-taxonomy.md` (built on the retired axis layer), `architecture/project-architecture-guidebook-v2.3.md`
(the claude.ai-surface architecture), `governance/project-instructions-v*.md`, and everything `.ignore` hides.

# CLAUDE.md audit: saliency and efficacy, with a proposed replacement

Written 2026-11-26 by a read-only Opus-class auditor for the owner's approval. Repository read at `origin/main` `71b7c58`. Nothing in the repository was edited. The proposed file is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/f8d4d6c2-8f72-53c6-8e31-d3258750c5f6/scratchpad/CLAUDE.proposed.md`. Line numbers ("L") are of the current `CLAUDE.md` at `71b7c58`; they drift, so locate by the quoted text.

**Owner's instruction (typed, 2026-11-26):** "please have Opus audit claude.md for saliency and efficacy. ensure we strip out all extraneous stuff like change logs and version discussion etc. we want to make sure that claude.md points correctly but also contains some strict rules of operation for us".

**Approval.** The ledger entry "Owner statements 2026-11-20 (third)" carries ACTION (1): "Do not rewrite `CLAUDE.md` until the owner approves the content above". The whole proposal therefore waits for the owner. Within it, OWNER-ONLY marks a change to the goal sentence, rule 0, rule 9, the tier and Co-1 definitions or the layer model (that entry: "The owner approves the goal sentence, rule 0, rule 9, the tier and Co-1 definitions, and the fate of the layer model"). DELEGABLE marks process wording, traps and command lists, which that entry says a session may reorder and reword. **Every OWNER-ONLY block is byte-identical in the proposed file.** The OWNER-ONLY changes are listed separately in section 2b and are not applied.

**Inputs reconciled.** `scratchpad/adjudication.md` (ADJ-), `scratchpad/adjudication-2.md` (ADJ2-), `scratchpad/antagonist-1.md` (its attack on ADJ-) and `scratchpad/ecosystem-census.md`. Where the antagonist overturned the first pass, this audit follows the antagonist: the seven-rank authority order of ADJ-04 is not applied (it ranks delegated resolutions above doctrine and CLAUDE.md, against the owner's "as always refer to doctrine/mission/claude.md etc for guidance as required", ledger "Owner statements 2026-11-25"), and the synthesis floor uses "Opus-class or above", not a closed list.

## Size, measured (re-run; do not trust the figures)

| Measure | Command |
|---|---|
| Current words | `wc -w < CLAUDE.md` (5809 at `71b7c58`) |
| Proposed words | `wc -w < /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/f8d4d6c2-8f72-53c6-8e31-d3258750c5f6/scratchpad/CLAUDE.proposed.md` (4040 when written) |
| The rewrite spec's target (unratified, not binding) | `echo $(( $(git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md \| wc -w) / 4 ))` (1452) |
| Words in OWNER-ONLY verbatim blocks | about 800 (goal, simplicity sentence, the three things, rule 0, rule 9, the layer quote, the tier and Co-1 lines) |

The quarter target cannot be met while rules 0 to 10, §3, §7 and §8 stay in CLAUDE.md: the OWNER-ONLY text alone is more than half of it. It is reachable only by the rewrite spec's move of those rules into a separate working-rules file, which the same ledger entry reserves to the owner (item O-09). This proposal keeps every rule in place and every number unchanged, and cuts history, proofs, duplicates and stale claims.

## Why the numbering is kept

Rule and section numbers are cited by number across the tree, including immutable migrations, executable scripts, the check registry, slash commands and skills. Sweep command (approximate: a bare "rule N" can belong to another numbering): `git grep -n -E 'CLAUDE\.md[^a-z]*(rule|section|§)|CLAUDE.md §|rule [0-9]+[a-c]?\b' -- scripts governance skills .claude decisions architecture | wc -l` (938 lines at `71b7c58`). The tally by token is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/f8d4d6c2-8f72-53c6-8e31-d3258750c5f6/scratchpad/rulecallers_tally.txt`. Several earlier renumberings already broke callers that were never repaired (section 3e). Any renumbering repeats that. The proposal keeps rules 0, 1–7, 7a, 8–10, sections §1–§9 and the labels §5(a), (b), (c).

Two callers parse CLAUDE.md mechanically, and both still pass on the proposed file (emulated, since the repository was not edited):
- `scripts/audit/claude_md_spine.py` (blocking): exactly one line matching `^\s*SPINE:` and equal to `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml` `stages:`. Emulated: one line, equal.
- `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py` (T126-30) reads `\bT(\d)[–-]T6\*\* the regulatory stratum` from CLAUDE.md. Emulated: matches, tier 4. **This is a second content pin that no document mentions;** the tier line must keep the literal "**T4–T6** the regulatory stratum".

## 2. Itemised change list

Convention: a short current text is quoted whole; a long one is quoted by its first and last words with its line range. Every DELEGABLE item below is applied in the proposed file.

### 2a. DELEGABLE changes (applied in the proposed file)

- Proposed: the same text, verbatim, placed after the three things never to be got wrong.
